topic: Rational cubic identification and correction of the one-proxy LvLiNGAM boundary. Observe iid X=(X1,X2,X3) from X=(I-B)^(-1)(gamma H+D_s xi), where B is one of six labeled positive two-edge chains, edge coefficients and global loadings lie in [1/4,3/4], residual scales lie in [3/4,5/4], and the four independent centered sources have support in [-2,2], variance one and third cumulant in [1/2,1]. Prove that C3 alone globally identifies the chain and both coefficients: the unique rank-two cubic slice identifies the root, its signed kernel identifies the middle, and explicit adjugate contractions recover both edges with uniform denominator bounds. On the exact Tramontano-Kivva-Salehkaleybar-Drton-Kiyavash one-proxy graph, reproduce and saturate the released Macaulay2 elimination, reconcile Theorem 3.6, and characterize genuine nonidentification versus removable chart failures outside the positive chamber. Prove covariance-only opposite-chain overlap on a nonempty open set. Give a constant-time rational algorithm and bounded-data moment-inversion confidence set with uniform finite-sample coverage and root-n diameter on denominator-separated subclasses, without requiring nonsingular influence covariance. Consumer: replace the fourth-cumulant proxy branch in CEId-from-Moments by a certified cubic branch on the positive-skew class, with ambiguity warnings on the audited failure divisor. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent algebra derived M_a=hx gg'+r dd', kernel k=(-uz,z+vy,-y), N=hxr(uyz,-y(z+vy),y^2), W=-hxrt yz(0,1,v), and the rational edge formulas; it also derived slice determinants and uniform denominators. Exact arithmetic recovered u=1/2,v=2/5 in the legal Bernoulli witness, 1,200 numerical relabelings passed, and an interior reversal-symmetric covariance witness had an invertible nuisance Jacobian. The released covariance equations and 60 cubic residual equations were reconstructed; a linear elimination certificate and localized generic degree one were derived. Hoeffding moment rectangles yielded honest inversion and root-n diameter without covariance inversion. Same-box twins, scaling, source permutations, graph-transpose conventions, zero denominators, negative-sign failures, singular moment covariance, bounded-source realizability were checked; no correction or collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Classify all real coefficient/order fibers outside the positive box, especially intersections of rank and denominator hypersurfaces, separating genuine ambiguity from removable adjugate-chart failures. EARLY KILL TEST: Run the pinned Macaulay2 file, reduce beta*W_b-W_c against its full elimination ideal, and localize at W_b; a nonzero remainder or retained generic second full-system root stops the correction claim. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_proxychain_cubic_inverse.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the third-cumulant tensor alone globally identifies the labeled chain and both direct effects in the three-observable, one-global-confounder LvLiNGAM when all edges, loadings, and source skewnesses are bounded away from zero and positive.

source_refs.claim: For the one-latent proxy-to-treatment graph, Theorem 3.6 finds a generically two-valued causal-effect fiber from cumulants through order three over the unconstrained real parameter space.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, and Negar Kiyavash
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267

source_refs.claim: The paper derives closed-form higher-cumulant recovery for a one-latent-component mixing structure, but not a positive-chamber cubic inverse for all six labeled three-node chains.
source_refs.author: Ruichu Cai, Zhiyi Huang, Wei Chen, Zhifeng Hao, and Kun Zhang
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published obstruction is algebraic and generic over an unconstrained real parameter space: elimination leaves the target as a root of a degree-two polynomial. It does not decide whether the second branch necessarily exits the compact positive-sign chamber or whether rank and signed-kernel geometry make the chain label recoverable. The missing steps are a semialgebraic branch-exclusion proof and certification that every adjugate contraction used to recover the edges has a uniform nonzero denominator. Targeted searches found fourth-order proxy results and broader cumulant/OICA algorithms, but no theorem for this third-cumulant-only positive six-chain class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A global target-identification theorem on the stated compact positive class, with an explicit rational map from the third-cumulant tensor to the root, middle node, and two edge coefficients and uniform lower bounds for all denominators.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the closest-written proxy-LvLiNGAM paper and frames lower-order cumulants as the identification boundary to revisit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding defeats covariance identification -> higher cumulants restore causal-effect information with one proxy -> the published real-unconstrained cubic fiber is quadratic -> positivity and labeled-chain geometry may collapse that fiber to a rational singleton.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the one-latent-component cumulant-slice factorization and its closed-form extraction proof, replacing generic OICA recovery with rank-two slice and signed-kernel arguments specialized to a chain.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems decompose an observed higher-cumulant tensor into one dense latent rank-one component plus structured idiosyncratic components.

method_exemplars.technique: Use elimination ideals and localized Gröbner-basis certificates to distinguish rational identification, generic finite identification, and genuine nonidentification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The correction must show why the published quadratic fiber disappears after semialgebraic restrictions without confusing localization failure with a second admissible model.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt low-order moment-tensor perturbation analysis to bound errors in the recovered cubic slice, kernel direction, and rational contractions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The identifying objects are spectral features of a third-order moment tensor, so their empirical stability is the natural estimation rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify every real parameter fiber of the one-latent, three-observable proxy-chain model outside the positive chamber, including intersections of cubic-rank and adjugate-denominator hypersurfaces, and separate genuine observational twins from failures of a chosen rational chart.

source_refs.claim: The one-proxy analysis reports a degree-two elimination equation for the causal effect at order three but does not stratify the full real exceptional locus.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, and Negar Kiyavash
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267

source_refs.claim: Elimination can certify generic identification properties, but a generic certificate does not enumerate semialgebraic real fibers on exceptional divisors.
source_refs.author: Luis David García-Puente, Sarah Spielvogel, and Seth Sullivant

open_problems.why_unsolved: A localized degree-one certificate controls only the chart where its denominator is nonzero, while a generic degree-two calculation suppresses sign restrictions and lower-dimensional components. At a rank-drop or denominator-zero intersection, a failed adjugate formula may indicate an alternative usable minor, a finite set of genuine twins, or a positive-dimensional fiber. Distinguishing these cases requires saturation and primary decomposition combined with real-feasibility analysis; the scan found no real semialgebraic fiber stratification for this model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite semialgebraic stratification of the real coefficient-loading-scale space with the observational moment map's fiber cardinality and chain-order content stated on every stratum, rational formulas on removable-chart strata, and explicit parameter twins on every genuine ambiguity stratum.

writing_exemplar.why: Its one-proxy theorems and released Macaulay2 calculation define the exact algebraic boundary whose real geometry must be completed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher cumulants yield generic proxy identification -> third-order elimination leaves an apparent quadratic ambiguity -> localization may remove one branch only off a divisor -> a complete result must classify that divisor and every real fiber on it.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt effect-coordinate elimination and ideal-membership certificates, adding chart-by-chart saturation before reading off fiber degree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution refines generic computer-algebra identification into an exact statement about the target coordinate on every component.

method_exemplars.technique: Mirror the distinction between global and generic injectivity, proving necessity with explicit fiber transformations and sufficiency by ruling them out.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is a global fiber theorem rather than a generic-identifiability statement, now for a higher-moment latent LiNGAM map.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a bounded-data confidence set for the labeled chain and its two direct causal effects obtained by rational cubic moment inversion that has finite-sample uniform coverage over the full compact model and root-n diameter on denominator-separated subclasses, even when empirical-moment influence covariance is singular.

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies cumulant-based point estimators and calls for more detailed uncertainty assessment, but gives neither finite-sample coverage nor singular-covariance-robust confidence sets.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, and Negar Kiyavash
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267

source_refs.claim: SR-AR and SR-CQLR give uniformly valid asymptotic inference for nonlinear moment models while allowing singular covariance, but not bounded-data finite-sample inversion over a union of rational LvLiNGAM charts.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Patrik Guggenberger

source_refs.claim: Concentration inequalities can yield honest confidence sets with uniform coverage and controlled diameter in inverse problems when CLT-based inference is unavailable.
source_refs.author: Andrii Babii

open_problems.why_unsolved: Plug-in delta-method intervals are not uniform near the rational failure divisor and can be undefined when influence covariance is singular; selecting among six chain labels adds a discrete nonregular step. A finite-sample route must form a simultaneous concentration rectangle for all second- and third-order moments of bounded observations, invert the exact polynomial relations over every label, and prove that denominator separation contracts the feasible parameter projection at rate n^{-1/2}. Existing one-proxy estimators report empirical error, while singularity-robust moment tests are asymptotic and concentration-based inverse-problem results do not treat this finite union of rational causal charts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicitly computable set-valued estimator obtained by inverting simultaneous bounded-moment inequalities, with nonasymptotic coverage uniform over the model and O(n^{-1/2}) high-probability diameter on subclasses whose identifying minors and branch-separation margins exceed a fixed positive constant.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates practical one-proxy cumulant estimation and identifies uncertainty assessment as missing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher cumulants identify effects unavailable from covariance -> closed-form estimators make the method implementable -> rational denominators and label selection create nonregular uncertainty -> honest inversion is needed before certified causal conclusions are possible.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the concentration-inequality construction and its coverage-plus-diameter proof, replacing the regularized inverse operator with exact inversion of a finite empirical-moment rectangle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both are inverse problems in which honesty must be established without invertible asymptotic covariance or a pointwise delta method.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singularity-robust test inversion and projection onto the nondegenerate moment span to retain validity when moment covariance loses rank.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed set must remain meaningful in the singular and near-singular moment-covariance regimes handled by SR-AR and SR-CQLR.

method_exemplars.technique: Use tensor perturbation inequalities to turn simultaneous third-moment error into quantitative errors for slice rank, kernel direction, and recovered coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the deterministic stability bridge between a concentration rectangle for the cubic tensor and root-n contraction of the causal parameter set.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize covariance-only observational equivalence among the six labeled positive two-edge chains with one dense latent factor, including which opposite-chain covariance images overlap on nonempty relatively open sets and the inequalities defining those overlaps.

source_refs.claim: LF-HTC gives sufficient criteria for rational recovery of direct effects from covariance in known explicit-latent graphs, but not pairwise covariance-image overlap when the chain label is unknown.
source_refs.author: Rina Foygel Barber, Mathias Drton, Nils Sturma, and Luca Weihs

source_refs.claim: The paper formalizes distribution equivalence and quasi-equivalence as observational limits on structure learning in linear directed models, motivating image-level rather than within-graph comparison.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Alan Yang, Negar Kiyavash, and Kun Zhang
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 119

source_refs.claim: Latent-variable LiNGAM can recover causal-order information while effects remain set-valued, but the positive one-factor three-node family's covariance-only overlaps are not isolated.
source_refs.author: Saber Salehkaleybar, AmirEmad Ghassami, Negar Kiyavash, and Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known-graph covariance identifiability and distribution equivalence for broader directed models do not determine whether differently labeled chain parameterizations have full-dimensional covariance-image intersections after imposing one dense latent factor and positive boxes. The first proof step must change from solving one graph's covariance equations to forming the fiber product of two chain-specific covariance maps. An interior witness and a full-rank nuisance Jacobian would establish open overlap, while elimination and real inequalities would describe its boundary. Targeted searches found fixed-graph half-trek criteria and general distribution-equivalence work, but no pairwise semialgebraic overlap theorem for this family.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic characterization of every pairwise intersection of the six covariance-model images, including an explicit interior opposite-chain witness and a submersion or Jacobian theorem proving that its overlap contains a nonempty relatively open set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its structure-versus-distribution-equivalence framing motivates why unknown chain labels require comparison of whole observational images.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional-independence equivalence can miss distributional information -> structure learning is limited by overlap of model images -> explicit latent-factor restrictions change those images -> pairwise covariance overlap must be characterized before cubic information can be credited with resolving order.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt rational covariance recovery for explicit latent-factor graphs to parameterize each chain image and expose residual nuisance degrees of freedom before comparing labels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same dense latent factor is represented explicitly, and the overlap theorem begins from the corresponding rational covariance equations.

method_exemplars.technique: Use graph-indexed parameter-map injectivity and explicit transformations between fibers to distinguish within-graph identification from cross-graph observational equivalence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required result is a global statement about covariance-map fibers and image intersections, the algebraic-geometric level at which global SEM identifiability is analyzed.

literature_map:
Shimizu et al. (2006, JMLR) establish full LiNGAM recovery from non-Gaussianity without hidden confounding.
Hoyer et al. (2008, IJAR, DOI:10.1016/j.ijar.2008.02.006) extend recovery to hidden-variable LiNGAM through overcomplete ICA.
Salehkaleybar et al. (2020, JMLR, arXiv:1908.03932) recover causal-order information and compatible effect sets under latent LiNGAM.
Adams, Hansen, and Zhang (2021, NeurIPS) give graphical conditions for partially observed non-Gaussian linear-model identification.
Wang and Drton (2023, JMLR) study structure recovery with unobserved confounding in bow-free acyclic path diagrams.
Kivva, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2306.06263) identify a one-proxy causal effect through cross moments but do not supply coverage theory.
Cai et al. (2023, ICML, arXiv:2305.19582) derive closed-form higher-cumulant recovery for one-latent-component mixtures.
Chen et al. (2024, AAAI, arXiv:2312.11934) use higher cumulants and asymmetry to orient an observed pair sharing one latent parent.
Tramontano et al. (2024, ICML, arXiv:2406.02049) characterize generic direct and total-effect identifiability in LvLiNGAM.
Tramontano et al. (2025, ICML, arXiv:2506.05202) treat the exact one-proxy graph; Theorem 3.6 leaves a quadratic effect fiber through order three over unrestricted real parameters.
García-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010, UAI, arXiv:1007.3784) provide elimination-ideal tests for causal-effect identifiability.
Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/10-AOS859) distinguish global from generic SEM identifiability; Barber et al. (2022, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/22-AOS2221) give rational covariance recovery with explicit latent factors.
Ghassami et al. (2020, ICML, arXiv:1910.12993) frame structure uncertainty through distribution and quasi-equivalence but do not analyze positive one-factor chain intersections.
Anandkumar et al. (2014, JMLR, arXiv:1210.7559) supply third-order tensor perturbation machinery; Babii (2020, Econometric Theory, arXiv:1611.03015) supplies concentration-based honest inverse-problem sets.
Andrews and Guggenberger (2019, Quantitative Economics, DOI:10.3982/QE1219) provide singularity-robust nonlinear-moment test inversion; the unoccupied junction is finite-sample bounded-moment inversion over rational cubic LvLiNGAM charts.
